title: Console Lite: Cost Attribution Sampler — MVP Pruning & Acceptance Criteria
creator: Maya Chen
description: Short PRD: Reduce Console surface for initial observability MVP by shipping a lightweight, probabilistic cost-attribution sampler and a single 'Route Cost' dashboard card. Goal is to deliver useful cost signals with <20% uplift in console latency and within the smallest engineering scope possible.
rationale: We cannot deliver full token-level cost accounting and full-span tracing within this cycle. A sampled, asynchronously aggregated cost pipeline preserves signal for product/engineer decisions while avoiding heavy storage and UI complexity. This reduces implementation time by ~60% vs full solution and enables progressive enhancement.
scope_in: API: per-route cost summary endpoint (sampled totals)
Console UI: single Route Cost card with top-5 routes and percent change
Trace: lightweight sampler hook that tags spans with route id and sample flag
Rollout: feature-flagged canary to 10% of orgs then ramp
scope_out: High-cardinality per-user cost dimensions in MVP
Interactive trace waterfall UI for the first release
Historical token decay modeling and per-model GPU delta heatmaps
acceptance_criteria: Route Cost card shows top 5 routes with sampled cost and delta vs baseline for last 24h (no P0 bugs blocking render)
API returns sampled cost totals with documented sampling rate header; sampling header present in >=95% of responses during test rollout
End-to-end pipeline processes sampled events on the canary org with latency < 2s for aggregation job (95th percentile) and no data loss observed in canary
Feature flag can be toggled and the system falls back to 'disabled' cleanly (UI displays 'cost unavailable' state)
Telemetry and alerts: alert fires if sampled ingest drop >5% or aggregation job fails two consecutive runs
Documentation: Confluence PRD + public SDK notes added and link included in ticket
milestones: PRD sign-off and acceptance criteria agreed (done)
Ramp to 100% or iterate based on canary feedback (week 6)
notes: 2025-11-03 Maya Chen: Kickoff — aligned with runtime team to accept sampled cost tags to avoid per-request enrichment in the serving path. Refer to confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/CL-ATTR-SAMPLER-PRD
2025-11-04 Evan Rodriguez: Tradeoff meeting — agreed to cap sampling rate at 10% for initial rollout; tradeoff is ~sqrt variance on low-frequency routes but acceptable for top-route ranking

2025-11-05 Priya Singh (Eng Lead): Implementation note — will implement sampling as a stochastic header injected in front proxy to avoid touching model runtime hot path; see draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4892
2025-11-07 Design feedback (A. Liu): Card layout must gracefully degrade to 'no data' state and include clear UX for sampling explanation and 'why sampling affects absolute numbers' microcopy
2025-11-09 QA update (J. Morales): Integration test found rare race where aggregation job double-counted events if retry policy overlaps; fixed by adding idempotency key (PR linked above)
2025-11-10 PM decision: Ship with scoped observability runbook and two follow-ups: (1) per-route sampling tuning, (2) evaluation job to compare sampled totals vs full ingest on subset of orgs
